title: After Basie: Herbie Fields, Jazz at the Philharmonic, Buddy Rich
summary: On leaving Basie he joined the New York union, then played with Herbie Fields, Jazz at the Philharmonic and Buddy Rich's small band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, what did you do when you left Basie?

Well, when I left Basie in '50, the first thing I had to do was join 802, because we were a traveling band all those years. None of us was a member of 802 but New York musicians like Dicky Wells, Benny Morton and guys like that that lived in New York, had to join the union. And then I went with Buddy Rich. No, first I went with Herbie Fields.
Yes, that was a small band, wasn't it?

Small band. Went with Herbie Fields and then I played around Philadelphia and New York, Providence, Rhode Island, all around the East Coast. Then I went with Jazz at the Philharmonic. I did that for about two years. Because it only lasted about six weeks a year at that time, anyway, you know, steady. So then I joined Buddy Rich's small band. We played at the Pop City, Royal Roost, played at Philadelphia, the Strand in Boston, around the East Coast, every place, you know. Zoot Sims and I were roommates. He had two horns, tenor and trumpet. Let's see, we had Rocky Calucci on piano who was the musical director for Patty Page for years, you know. And, oh, I don't know, I can't think of other guys -- the bass player.
But Zoot and I, we played with Buddy for a long time. And then I free lanced around New York, played the Apollo with different bands like Stan Getz, when he had a band to go in there.
